modern:
When Jesus gave himself for us, he gave us all the rights and privileges that went with himself. As the eternal God, he has rights belonging to his very nature that no creature may dare to claim. But as Jesus, the Mediator, the head who represents us in the covenant of grace, he has no inheritance apart from us. All the glorious results of his obedience to death are the shared wealth of all who are in him, for whom he carried out God’s will. Look, he enters glory, but not for himself alone, for it’s written, “Whither the Forerunner is *for us* entered” ([[Heb.6.20|Hebrews 6:20]]). Does he stand in the presence of God? “He appears in the presence of God *for us*” ([[Heb.9.24|Hebrews 9:24]]).

Think about this, believer. You have no right to heaven in yourself. Your right lies in Christ. If you’re pardoned, it’s through *his* blood. If you’re justified, it’s through *his* righteousness. If you’re made holy, it’s because God has made *him* your holiness. If you’re kept from falling, it will be because you’re kept safe in Christ Jesus. And if you’re made perfect at the end, it will be because you’re complete in *him*. So Jesus is honored, because everything is in him and by him. So the inheritance is made sure for us, because it’s obtained in him. And so every blessing is sweeter, and even heaven itself is brighter, because it’s Jesus our Beloved “in whom” we’ve obtained it all.

Who can put a value on our divine inheritance? Weigh Christ’s riches on scales and his treasure in balances, and then think of counting the treasures that belong to the saints. Reach the bottom of Christ’s sea of joy, and then hope to understand the happiness God has prepared for those who love him. Leap over the boundaries of Christ’s estates, and then dream of a limit to the lovely inheritance of God’s chosen. “All things are yours, for ye are Christ’s and Christ is God’s.”

modern:
It will always give a Christian the deepest calm, quiet, ease and peace to think about the perfect righteousness of Christ. How often God’s people are downcast and sad! I don’t think they ought to be. I don’t think they would be if they could always see their perfection in Christ. Some people are always talking about corruption, and the sinfulness of the heart, and the evil we’re born with. That’s all quite true, but why not go a little further and remember that we are “perfect in Christ Jesus”? No wonder those who dwell on their own corruption look so downcast. But surely if we remember that “Christ is made unto us righteousness,” we’ll cheer up.

So what if troubles afflict me and Satan attacks me, and there may be many things to go through before I get to heaven? Those things are taken care of for me in the covenant of God’s grace. Nothing is lacking in my Lord: Christ has done it all. On the cross he said, “It is finished!” and if it is finished, then I am complete in him and can rejoice with joy too great for words and full of glory, “Not having mine own righteousness, which is of the law, but that which is through the faith of Christ, the righteousness which is of God by faith.”

You won’t find a holier people this side of heaven than those who take the teaching of Christ’s righteousness into their hearts. When a believer says, “I live on Christ alone; I rest on him solely for salvation; and I believe that, however unworthy, I am still saved in Jesus;” then this thought rises up as a reason for gratitude: “Shall I not live to Christ? Shall I not love him and serve him, seeing that I am saved by his merits?” “The love of Christ constraineth us,” “that they which live should not henceforth live unto themselves but unto him which died for them.” If we’re saved by righteousness credited to us, we’ll greatly value the righteousness worked in us.

modern:
Running isn’t everything. A lot depends on the route we choose. A fast runner going up hill and down dale won’t keep up with a slower traveler on level ground. How is it with my spiritual journey? Am I struggling up the hill of my own works and down into the ravines of my own humiliations and resolutions? Or do I run by the plain way of “Believe and live”? How blessed it is to wait on the Lord by faith! The soul runs without getting tired and walks without fainting on the road of believing. Christ Jesus is the way of life, and he is a plain way, a pleasant way, a way that suits the tottering feet and weak knees of trembling sinners. Am I on this road, or am I hunting for some other track that priestcraft or philosophy might promise me? I read of the way of holiness, that the traveler, though a fool, won’t go astray on it. Have I been rescued from proud reason and brought like a little child to rest in Jesus’ love and blood? If so, by God’s grace I’ll outrun the strongest runner who chooses any other path.

I’d do well to remember this truth in my daily worries and needs. The wisest course will be to go straight to my God, and not to wander in a roundabout way to this friend and that one. He knows what I need and can supply it. Who should I turn to but him, by the direct appeal of prayer and the plain argument of the promise? “Straightforward makes the best runner.” I won’t haggle with the servants, but hurry to their master.

As I read this passage, it strikes me that if people compete with each other in ordinary things, and one outruns the other, I ought in all seriousness to run so as to win. Lord, help me to get my mind ready for action, and to press on toward the goal for the prize of God’s high calling in Christ Jesus.
